one_liner: Senior FinCEN regulatory writer who drafts and reviews Bank Secrecy Act anti-money-laundering regulations and guidance, working closely with Treasury lawyers.
fit_summary: Daniel's policy knowledge, people skills and IEM consulting background are real assets, but this GS-13/14 role requires a year of specialized experience analyzing or writing AML, CFT or financial-crimes regulations at the GS-12/13 level. Unless Daniel's IEM work involved regulatory analysis of financial-crimes or closely similar laws, Daniel is unlikely to be rated qualified.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens or nationals) under Direct-Hire authority; no federal status needed and veterans' preference does not apply.

GS-13: one year of specialized experience at GS-12 level analyzing statutes/regulations or reviewing, interpreting or writing regulations or guidance related to AML, CFT, financial crimes, or similar laws.
GS-14: the GS-13 experience plus coordinating and implementing AML/CFT/financial-crimes programs, policies and operations, at GS-13 level.
No degree required, but you must pass a Moderate Risk Public Trust Tier 2 background investigation, Continuous Vetting, FBI Rap Back and an ethics/financial-interest review.
Must complete the questionnaire and the USA Hire online assessment by the cut date you target.
strategy: Before applying, honestly check whether any IEM work involved reading, interpreting or applying federal statutes and regulations, such as the Stafford Act, 2 CFR 200 or FEMA Public Assistance rules. Only claim those under 'similar laws' if you truly did that work, and expect HR may judge them not similar enough.

Apply at GS-13 only, since you have no AML program coordination experience for GS-14. Answer the self-assessment questionnaire truthfully; inflated answers that your resume doesn't support lead to 'not qualified' ratings.

Keep the resume to two pages. List month/day/year dates and hours per week for each job, and put a concise specialized-experience bullet near the top of the IEM entry that uses posting language like 'analyzing statutes and regulations' and 'regulatory guidance'.
Target the earliest cut date (11/02/2026), or at latest 12/18/2026, rather than the 02/02/2027 close. Prepare for the USA Hire assessment, which tests reading comprehension, reasoning and judgment.
Write the optional four 200-word mission essays to show your policy knowledge and commitment to the rule of law, and opt in to sharing with other Treasury bureaus.
Treat this as a stretch application, and also pursue better-fit roles in FEMA, Virginia VDEM, NoVA county emergency management, or legislative offices, where your background aligns directly.
resume_bullets: Analyzed [federal statute/regulation, e.g., 2 CFR 200 or Stafford Act provisions] for [government client] to [interpret compliance requirements/draft guidance], producing [number/type of products] for [audience] ([hours]/week).

Drafted and reviewed [policy memos/guidance documents/procedures] for [client agency], ensuring tone, clarity and accuracy for [intended audience] and coordinating legal or leadership review with [stakeholders].
Coordinated implementation of [program/policy] across [number] [state/local/federal] stakeholders, briefing [officials] and resolving [issue type] to achieve [result you can document].
interview_questions: Walk us through a time you interpreted a complex statute or regulation and turned it into practical guidance.
How would you balance regulatory burden on financial institutions against law-enforcement needs when drafting a BSA rule?
Describe how you worked with attorneys or reviewers to get a document cleared and resolved disagreements.
Tell us about a time you influenced stakeholders who initially opposed a policy recommendation.
watch_outs: The AML/CFT/financial-crimes specialized experience requirement is the main barrier; emergency-management experience will likely not count unless it clearly involved analyzing comparable regulations.
Applications are reviewed in batches at cut dates (11/02/2026, 12/18/2026, 02/02/2027), so applying late may mean the positions are already filled.
Tier 2 Public Trust investigation, Continuous Vetting and the financial conflict-of-interest review are conditions of employment.
The job is in DC and is not remote, so expect a commute from Manassas on office days despite telework eligibility.
